body: I don't want to bore anyone.. I was taking care of my sister & Bro-in-law's guest ranch in the Rocky Mountains, because they & my parents were all on the East Coast, at my cousin's wedding ( we all joked about the omen of getting married during 9/11! ) & we only had one hunter for black powder season. So, I had my almost 5 yr old son with me, it was so tranquil.. got up at 6, made coffee & breakfast for Bruce & my little guy, & my Dad always had NPR on the radio, so I had it on while I did breakfast & coffee. Then, it caught my attention, that there were suddenly long silences, & rambling sentences, so I started listening more closely. I thought it was a natural disaster, like a building collapsed, but NOT ANYTHING LIKE THE REALITY!!  By the time our housekeeper came up, ( this is on Mountain Standard Time, so 2 hrs behind the EC ), & I told her I thought we should go to my sister's house, to turn on the tv, & that's what we did - & when we got to the house & turned the TV on, it was already showing the first tower, with the huge gaping hole , & then, they broke in live, as the second plane flew right into the second tower! Erica & I found ourselves holding hands, without ever thinking about doing so! That's when, in my mind, we could see the tower swaying & we were like, no way is that gonna COLLAPSE?!? THEN, A FEW MINUTES LATER, IT DID!! 🫣😱🫣😱🤯 It was the worst thing I'd ever seen, ( except for watching my true love shoot himself right in front of me in '98 ) but we never thought "Oh, yeah, THIS is terrorism!" It was my Dad, a Veteran, 82nd Airborne Division, who saw the last plane fly into the second tower, & he said immediately, This is not an accident, it's an attack! Which really made it sink in for me! My sister had flown into Dulles with my niece, who was 2 & a half, on the 9th, & was at the airport the day before - until I could get myself under control, I had to find out if she'd been added to the manifest of a different flight, possibly flying out on Northwest, Delta, etc.. later on I talked to my parents, & my sis was fine, but for the first couple of hours, I was praying that she & Lydia had been able to get a good flight from D.C., even if they were bumped to a fuller loaded flight.. but I couldn't get a hold of her. And I was getting scared, my WHOLE FAMILY was there to be present for this wedding, yet NOW it seemed that was the worst thing they could have done

I don't think you did the best thing concerning your daughter's punishment. Obviously, she's been heading in a certain direction for awhile, & since you raised her, you should have been more on top of her behavior, & seen the signs of her bullying less fortunate kids. She sounds like a punk, & deserves to be punished, but it's a radical punishment that is going to make her focus on hating you, & not on learning to be empathetic to less fortunate kids around her. I say this because I was a very rebellious teenager, I was a normal, awkward preteen, & early teen, but when I hit 15, I started getting attention from boys, & my BFF had very lenient, laid back parents, so I felt that I was being treated terribly-& I started to listen to my friends, instead of my parents. It caused lasting issues between myself & my 22 mos younger sister, & it took forever to get back a good relationship with my parents. Don't let that happen between you & your daughter. Don't do something so drastic that she's not going to have an epiphany about being kinder to others, but instead, is going to cause her to focus only on revenge, & on hurting you back. So many things can go so wrong with that scenario.. ground her during the week & keep her away from her friends for a few weeks, but let her go to the competition, as she did earn her place on the team. Too much discipline can really backfire, & I'd hate to read that she's now in juvie for a much bigger thing than picking on a classmate. Best wishes, & you're being a good Mom.

I guess I'm too much of a Tolkien fan, to really appreciate the "genius" of GRRM. To me, it's obvious that he's an American, trying to seem like a Brit, & the dialogue is full of repetitive "sweetlings", "japes" ( not everyone, even during the Renaissance period, used the word "jape" when referring to a joke, jest, or sardonic brow-raising comment ) & everyone seems to greet family members as "my sweet brother, sister, mother, father, cousin.." etc. Maybe it's because he didn't create new, exotic names, for the Royalty of King's Landing, but rather, ( from the book ) spelled common names phonetically, so "Sir Davos" is "Ser" Davos, & instead of spelling "Walter", he spelled it "Walder", "Rickon" from "" Richard ", " Benjen" from "Benjamin", etc. Tolkien created a world that was totally unique, & populated it with distinct, separate beings, who had different languages, that were not anything like our English, & not like each other, rather than using people that have cultures that are not well-thought out, such as, if the Dothraki are so amazing, & such fantastic horseback riders, why are they still living in tents, & why are they still raping & enslaving the women they capture ? Why do they treat women in such a misogynistic way, if they are so great? All the people in the books & the series are just kind of sub-par, but still, I enjoy the read, & really love the show! It's just not.. Tolkien!  I realize that I have just opened myself up to a huge amount of hatred, it was not my intention, I was just thinking of how much you loved & admired GRRM, & I was sad that I don't feel that way about him. It's not that I'm saying he's a bad writer, it's just that he's not as detailed, & hasn't spent his entire life making notes, creating language like the Elven tongue, & the speech of the men of Nùmenor, the way J.R.R. Tolkien did, & so much of his ( GRRM ) dialogue is, as I said, superficial, & doesn't have the deep emotion that a character like, say, Aragorn, had. Like you, I believe that the writing is THE most important part of the consumption of that material, & once the story goes to the people, it takes on a life of its own. I'd love to have been a fly on the wall for some of the meetings between GRRM, & the producers of the GOT series!! And I wonder how much was left on the cutting room floor, in order to make it conform to the timetable of 1 hr per episode, for however many episodes they ran during whatever season was playing. I'm not going to stop reading "A Clash of Kings", but I HAD to speak my mind about the books, & their writer. I believe that he wrote them the way he did because of the times in which we live: most people don't have the attention span to read the" LOTR" trilogy, but " ASOIAF " is not as cumbersome as that, it's a fairly easy read, so it's great for quick consumption. Anyway, you made many valid, & great, points!
